Agent.description: Agent is an agent of a tab: Num is its number in the tab, as the user sees it ("1:claude"); State as `nerdr agents` says it; Messages how many messages wait to be typed in to it.

AgentEvent.description: An agent's state changed: was is the state before, left out for an agent just come; agent.state is "gone" for one gone. name is its tab's.

Answer.description: Answer is the core's answer to a request, with the request's id: result, or error, a sentence for people. A line with only an error, before the welcome, is why the core refused the client. x-nerdr-ops gives each op's result.

AnswerRequest.description: Answer one of nerdr's questions by its ID; yes left out is no.

AnsweredEvent.description: A question is answered, here or in another client, or its time ran out.

commits_after_pr.description: commits_after_pr is how many commits the branch has on top of its merged or closed PR: work that went on after it, in no PR.

ClientLine.description: A line a client sends: hello first, then requests.

ClosePaneRequest.description: Close an agent or a terminal in a tab, stopping what runs in it, as the TUI does; an agent's conversation is kept. The tab's first agent, whose ID is the tab's, stays as long as the tab and is refused: close the tab with close_tab. The tab gets a tab event, or the agent an agent event. target is an agent's or a terminal's ID; agent works too, for an agent.

CloseTabRequest.description: Close a tab, stopping everything in it, and answer once it is closed. With remove its worktrees are deleted too, never by force: it is refused, the tab left open, if that would lose changes not committed or commits not pushed. The branches are kept, unless each one's pull request is merged with the head it has.

ClosedResult.description: ClosedResult is close_tab's result: what became of the tab, in a sentence for people.

CoreLine.description: A line the core sends: the welcome first, then answers and, once subscribed, events.

Event.description: What a subscribed client is told as it happens: a line with an event and no id.

Hello.description: Hello is what a client says first.

api.description: api is the version of the API the client was written for; 0 is taken as 1. A core of an older one refuses it.

LostEvent.description: The client read too slowly and events were dropped: get the state afresh.

NewAgentRequest.description: Start an agent of the kind named (one of state's agents) beside a tab's own, in a new pane, with model if given and task as its first message if given; nerdr's window keeps the keyboard where it is. It comes with an agent event.

NewTabRequest.description: Make a tab on a new branch in the repositories named, its agent (the first of state's agents when not given) started with task. The tab comes with a tab_opened event once its worktrees are made, or a notice says why not.

NewTabResult.description: NewTabResult is new_tab's result: the branch of the tab being made.

NewTerminalRequest.description: Open a terminal in a tab's worktree, in a new pane, last; nerdr's window keeps the keyboard where it is. The tab gets a tab event with the terminal.

NoticeEvent.description: What nerdr tells the user in its status bar; important for what it keeps on screen until seen.

OpenedResult.description: OpenedResult is new_terminal's and new_agent's result: the ID of the terminal or the agent started.

Question.description: Question is something nerdr asks the user, to answer yes or no by its ID. Kind is "repo_setup" (may the setup of Repos run in new worktrees) or "plugin_run" (may Agent run Plugin with Values, in Dir; unanswered by Until, it is no).

QuitRequest.description: Stop nerdr for its folder, as quitting in its window does: every agent, terminal and plugin stops, and the tabs are kept. The connection then closes, maybe before the answer comes.

ReadRequest.description: The last lines (80 if not given) of what an agent or a terminal shows, as plain text, the size of its screen, which the lines are laid out for, whether it is on the alternate screen (alt), and whether scroll works on it now (wheel). target is an agent's or a terminal's ID; agent works too, for an agent.

ReadResult.description: ReadResult is read's result: what the agent or terminal shows, and the size of its screen, which the text is laid out for; 0 when nothing runs.

alt.description: alt is true when the program is full-screen, on the alternate screen, which keeps no scrollback: the text is only what fits, the rest of its history the program's own.

wheel.description: wheel is true when scroll works now: the program is on the alternate screen and takes the mouse wheel. Left out by a nerdr without scroll.

Repo.description: Repo is a repository a tab can be made in.

ReposRequest.description: The repositories a tab can be made in.

Request.description: A line a client sends after hello: op, what to do, and the parameters it takes. id is any JSON value, sent back with the answer.

ReviewRequest.description: Start a code review of an agent's work by an agent of the kind by (the one the config gives when not given), with model if given; or add that reviewer to the review going on. The reviewer comes with an agent event once the worktree is looked at, or a notice says why not, such as there being nothing to review.

ScrollRequest.description: Turn the mouse wheel over a full-screen agent or terminal, which keeps its history itself: lines steps, up (to older text) when positive, down when negative, at most 50 either way (more is 50), 0 none. It works only while read says wheel; otherwise it is an error saying the program does not scroll, and nothing is sent. Viewed by this connection, the program gets the view's size first, as with type. target is an agent's or a terminal's ID; agent works too, for an agent.

SeenRequest.description: Count as the user looking at the agent, as visiting its tab does.

SendRequest.description: Queue text as a message for agent, typed in once it is at its prompt.

Spinoff.description: Spinoff is the parts a tab's agent sent to split off into new tabs, waiting for the user: Parts in the order they are gone through, only the first answered.

busy.description: busy says what is being made for the first part, while it is ("making fix-a…"): it cannot be answered meanwhile.

done.description: done is how many parts of the plan have been gone through already: the first of Parts is part Done+1 of Done+len(Parts).

failed.description: failed is why the tab for the first part was not made the last time it was tried, for the user to put right, such as a branch name taken.

SpinoffCreateRequest.description: Make the tab for part, the first of those a tab's agent split its work into (its spinoff in state), as the TUI's spinoff dialog does: on a new branch from origin's main, named branch (the part's when not given), with the agent kind (the part's kind when not given; one of its kinds), starting with the part's commits unless reuse is false, in the repositories named in repos (by their folder in the tab, or any that repos lists; when not given, those the agent asked for). It needs the part's prompt_ready. nerdr may first ask whether the repositories' setup may run (a repo_setup question); then spinoff.busy says the tab is being made, and a spinoff event comes once the part is gone through, its tab with a tab_opened event, or, when it could not be made (a branch name taken, say), with why in spinoff.failed, the part still first. Parts made on another machine are not the API's.

SpinoffEvent.description: The parts a tab's agent split its work into, waiting for the user (its spinoff in state), changed: they came, a part's prompt came, one was gone through, its tab began to be made, or could not be (failed). spinoff is null once none wait.

SpinoffFailed.description: SpinoffFailed is why a part's tab was not made: Branch is the name it was to have, Err why, in a sentence for people.

SpinoffPart.description: SpinoffPart is one part to split off: ID is what spinoff_create and spinoff_skip name it by, Branch the name the agent proposes, Summary what the user reads of it, Commits those in the tab's branch with its work already. Repos are the folders of the tab's repositories the agent named for it, InRepos, when it named none, those its commits are in. Sandboxed is set when an agent in a sandbox sent it: only an agent set sandboxed may run it. PromptReady is set once the agent has sent the prompt the new agent is to be given; the tab cannot be made before.

kinds.description: kinds are the agents that may run in its tab, and Kind the one picked when spinoff_create names none; "" when there is none.

SpinoffSkipRequest.description: Go past part, the first of those a tab's agent split its work into, with no tab made for it: the agent is told, and keeps the work. A spinoff event follows.

State.description: State is what the API's state gives: every tab, the agents that want the user, neediest first (as the waiting list has them), what nerdr asks the user, and the agents there are to start.

StateRequest.description: Every tab with its agents, terminals and branches, the agents that need the user, nerdr's open questions, and the agents that can be started.

SubscribeRequest.description: Have the core send events from now on.

Tab.description: Tab is a tab. Status is what its agent last said of where the work stands (nerdr status); Task what it was asked to do.

spinoff.description: spinoff is the parts its agent split its work into, waiting for the user to make a tab for each or skip it; left out when none wait. The agent is blocked meanwhile.

TabEvent.description: A tab's name, task, status, branches or terminals changed.

TabOpenedEvent.description: A tab is there, made by anyone. Its agents each get an agent event too.

Terminal.description: Terminal is a terminal pane of a tab: Name as `nerdr read` calls it, Command the last an agent ran in it.

TypeRequest.description: Type into an agent or a terminal now: text as a paste, then keys. Give text, keys or both. Viewed by this connection, the program gets the view's size.

UnviewRequest.description: Stop showing an agent or a terminal: the size of the client active in it before holds, or the size it has.

ViewRequest.description: Show an agent or a terminal at cols × rows (brought within 20–500 × 5–300): the client active in a program last, the one that viewed it first, typed to it, scrolled it or changed the size it shows it at, sets its size; the others show the same screen. Say it again within 60 seconds, every 20 as a rule, while it is shown, or the view runs out; it goes too when the connection closes. The result is the size the program has now, the view's own or that of a client active in it since. target is an agent's or a terminal's ID; agent works too, for an agent.

ViewResult.description: ViewResult is view's result: the size the agent's or terminal's program has now, the view's own or that of a client active in it since.

WaitingEvent.description: The agents that need the user changed: their IDs, neediest first.

WakeRequest.description: Wake the agents of a tab put to sleep while it was not looked at.

Welcome.description: Welcome is the core's answer to a hello it takes.

description: nerdr's API, version 1: JSON, one object a line, over nerdr api FOLDER or the API socket. What is added to a version (fields, ops, events) does not raise it, so a client must pass by what it does not know.
title: nerdr API
